name: Necho's Phoenicians sail round Africa
traveler: Phoenician sailors, for Pharaoh Necho II
summary: Pharaoh Necho sends Phoenician ships south from the Red Sea with orders to come home by the Pillars of Heracles. Each autumn they land, sow and wait for the harvest; in the third year they reach Egypt again. Herodotus did not believe their report that the noon sun stood on their right, which is the best evidence they told the truth.

stops.note: Necho, who has also begun a canal from the Nile to the Red Sea, sends them south.
Down the coast of eastern Africa.
They land, sow grain and wait for the harvest before sailing on.
Sailing west round the continent, they see the noon sun to the north, on their right hand.
Another landing, another harvest, on the Guinea coast.
Into the Mediterranean in the third year.
Home to Egypt. Their story reaches Herodotus a century and a half later.
